terminal.description: A shell that starts in the shop's top folder. Try each pattern with ls before you move anything with it.

tasks.title: Move every drawing into artwork
tasks.description:
Hesper's new drawings were saved into `downloads`, between invoices and lists. Move every `.svg` file in `downloads` into `artwork`, and nothing else.

Check looks for each drawing from `downloads` in `artwork`, checks that none is left in `downloads`, and fails if a file that is not a drawing ended up in `artwork`.
nextSteps: Run `ls downloads` and pick out the drawings by their ending.
Write a pattern that matches only those names, and try it with `ls`.
When `ls` lists exactly the drawings, use the same pattern with `mv`.
List both folders to see the result.
hints: Every drawing's name ends the same way. The lesson's `*` stands for any run of characters.
`ls downloads/*.svg` should list only the drawings. Then hand the same pattern to `mv`, with `artwork` last.
Run `mv downloads/*.svg artwork` from the top folder.

tasks.title: File the March invoices
tasks.description:
Three March invoices are in `downloads` too, among other `.csv` files that are not invoices. Move every file in `downloads` whose name starts with `invoice-` into `invoices/march`, and nothing else.

Check looks for each invoice from `downloads` in `invoices/march`, checks that none is left in `downloads`, and fails if a file that is not an invoice ended up in `invoices/march`.
nextSteps: Run `ls downloads/*.csv` and see why the ending alone is not enough here.
Write a pattern built on how the invoices' names start.
Try it with `ls`, then use it with `mv`.
hints: A pattern can fix the start of a name as well as its end.
Put the fixed part first and `*` after it. Test it with `ls` until only invoices show.
Run `mv downloads/invoice-* invoices/march` from the top folder.

tasks.title: Gather the Pellow Bakery orders
tasks.description:
Idris wants every order from Pellow Bakery together. Make a folder `pellow` inside `orders`, then move every file directly in `orders` whose name ends in `-pellow.txt` into it. Orders from other customers stay where they are, and the `2026` folder is left alone.

Check looks for each Pellow Bakery order in `orders/pellow`, checks that none is left loose in `orders`, and fails if another customer's order or anything from `2026` was moved.
nextSteps: Run `ls orders` and find what the Pellow Bakery orders have in common.
Try a pattern with `ls` that lists only the Pellow Bakery orders.
Move them with the same pattern, then list `orders` and `orders/pellow`.
hints: Their names differ at the start and agree at the end.
A `*` can come first: it matches the order numbers, and the fixed part after it picks the customer.
